solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 31 days of wind after seconds of lamb curry

indicators.note: the second letter of each of the words lamb and curry is taken

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind

explanation.surface: A month spent with flatulence brought on by a lamb curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the wind piece behind the two second letters. '31 days' looks like a span of time to be calculated but simply defines a month of that length.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month of the year has thirty-one days, so the length stands for the month.

clue.text: It's redolent of Emilia-Romagna

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the place name, so 'of' signals a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Something that brings to mind the scents of the northern Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the hyphen of Emilia-Romagna, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: a smell evoking the region.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell is what something redolent gives off, so a scent is the thing that is redolent.

clue.text: Astronomer from Italy aboard sailing ship briefly

indicators.note: the country's letter goes on board, inside the shortened ship
the ship's name is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a galleon is a large old sailing ship
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A stargazer leaves Italy on board a sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pisan scientist was the famous early telescope observer of Jupiter's moons, a celebrated stargazer.

clue.text: Scheme giving rise to huge pies

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: mega means huge, enormous
tarts are pies with fruit or other fillings

explanation.surface: A plan that leads to the baking of enormous pies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or ruse, a synonym for a scheme.

clue.text: Selfishness of horrible heartless moggies

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made horrible, jumbled into a new order
the middle letter of the word moggies is removed

explanation.surface: Nasty, cruel cats display selfishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central G of MOGGIES, leaving MOGIES, which 'horrible' rearranges. A moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is concern for one's own interests, the same as selfishness.

clue.text: Oink and tail of pig, smallest in litter

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here of pig

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal of a litter

explanation.surface: A piglet's noise and its curly tail, the weakling of the litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunt is its noise, written in comics as an oink.

clue.text: Bitterness of individual lines by the Bard

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single individual
L is the standard abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
the Bard is William Shakespeare, known as Will

explanation.surface: Resentment found in particular lines written by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bard' is Shakespeare, whose short name Will gives the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or resentment towards someone, a form of bitterness.

clue.text: Lawgiver hoards metals and prepares for war

indicators.note: the lawgiver keeps the metals stored within him

parts.note: Moses brought the Ten Commandments, the biblical lawgiver
Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth, a metal
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium, another metal

explanation.surface: A ruler stockpiles metal and gets ready for conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Two metals are needed: the chemical symbols for bismuth and lithium.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise is to assemble troops and make them ready for active service in wartime.

clue.text: People regularly ignored fat hornless animal

indicators.note: every other letter of the word people is skipped, keeping the first, third and fifth

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Folk often overlooked an overweight beast without horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollard is an animal, such as a stag or ox, that has lost or shed its horns.

clue.text: Left with dull baby, heads off for air at bedtime

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the words dull and baby is removed

explanation.surface: Left with a boring infant, people head off for some fresh air before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like fresh air but is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to send a child to sleep, a tune for bedtime.

clue.text: Go away and, without former husband, exude perfect happiness

parts.note: beat it is slang for go away

indicators.note: the word exude is to be taken without the former husband

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Telling someone to leave, then glowing with bliss once the ex is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude is supreme blessedness, a state of utter bliss.

clue.text: Elstree unoriginally invested in Disney movie of 1987

indicators.note: the cut-down studio name is placed inside the first name

parts.note: Walt Disney founded the Disney film company

indicators.note: the original, that is first, letter of Elstree is dropped

explanation.surface: A British studio puts money into a 1987 Disney picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree is a famous British film studio. 'invested' is the financial word fitting the answer, but signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Stone's 1987 film about financial greed, starring Michael Douglas, carries this title.

clue.text: Rosa Klebb would kick stuffing out of 9 for no particular reason

parts.note: Rosa Klebb is the setter, so the setter would becomes I'd

indicators.note: the inner letters of the answer to clue 9 are knocked out, leaving its ends

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a bedtime song

explanation.surface: The setter, a Bond villain's namesake, would kick a song to bits on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosa Klebb is the setter's pseudonym (after the kicking Bond villain), so 'Rosa Klebb would' is I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something idly means doing it without purpose, aimlessly.

clue.text: Run away from crowd in minuscule knickers

indicators.note: the run is taken away from the crowd

parts.note: a throng is a crowd
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fleeing a crowd while wearing very skimpy underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is skimpy underwear with only a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Surprisingly, Tinder has lost lustre

indicators.note: the letters arrive in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Remarkably, the dating app has lost its shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tarnished has become dull, its shine gone.

clue.text: Crass Celts sat around

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: Boorish Celtic people sat about.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass remarks are insensitive and lacking in tact.

clue.text: Seconds out, clubs and clouts lads who are prepared

indicators.note: the second letter of each of the words clubs and clouts is taken out

explanation.surface: A boxing referee's call, then blows with clubs and fists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds out' is the boxing call before a round, but here removes the second letter of each word. 'Be prepared' is the Scout motto.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior Scouts follow the movement's motto Be Prepared, so they are boys who are ready.

clue.text: Pass on Sumatran's mitre box

indicators.note: a box holds things inside, so the words contain the letters

explanation.surface: Handing on an Indonesian bishop's headdress in its case.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit something is to send or hand it on to another.

clue.text: Retired Missouri dons sound disgusting

indicators.note: the sound puts on the reversed state, as one dons clothing

parts.note: a noise is a sound

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri

explanation.surface: Retired Missouri academics sound revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but means puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling, so very unpleasant.

clue.text: Rude people show contempt for Royal Society

parts.note: to boo someone is to jeer them
RS stands for the Royal Society, the UK's science academy

explanation.surface: Ill-mannered folk jeer the scientific academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Boors are coarse, ill-mannered people.

clue.text: I force operative to fence off one hole

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form a fence around the single letter
the letters are put to work, operating in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker is made to put a fence round a single opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operative' looks like a worker noun but tells you to rearrange I FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, such as a mouth or vent.

clue.text: Five sons refused to kiss Swiss bird

indicators.note: the sons are turned away, taken out of the words

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son, and five are needed

explanation.surface: Five boys won't kiss a feathered Swiss creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The words kiss Swiss hold exactly five S's; removing them all leaves the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird.

clue.text: Point of sale?

parts.note: the shop till phrase is reread as the purpose of a sale, which is cutting prices

explanation.surface: The shop checkout where purchases are paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: Markdowns in price are the whole purpose of a sale.

clue.text: Regretting batting wearing toupee

indicators.note: the hairpiece has the batting piece inside it, as if worn

parts.note: rug is slang for a toupee
a batsman who is in is batting in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer sorry to be batting in a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, and this is the present participle.

clue.text: Hearing horseman when one sleeps

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound of the word for a mounted soldier

parts.note: a knight was a mounted warrior

explanation.surface: Hearing a rider approach while asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are the time people usually sleep.

clue.text: Very bad lad enthralled by elegance

indicators.note: the lad is held captive inside the elegance

parts.note: chic means stylishness or elegance
Ron is a boy's name, standing for any lad

explanation.surface: A dreadful young man is captivated by style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chronic' meaning very bad is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British use, chronic means dreadful or of very poor quality.

clue.text: Day trips from Tunis go wrong

indicators.note: the letters go wrong, ending up in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Excursions from the Tunisian capital fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short pleasure trips or excursions.

clue.text: Remove deposits from bed of Doctor Heidegger, oddly absent

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the philosopher's name are missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Clearing silt from the bed of a doctor named Heidegger, who is oddly not there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a riverbed or seabed. Heidegger was a German philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to scoop mud and silt from the bottom of a river or harbour.

clue.text: Reportedly sanction rise

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for agreement sounds like the entry

parts.note: assent is approval, a sanction

explanation.surface: Word is that approval was given for an increase.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward movement.
